context.title: Abrishami, Henning, and Rahbarnia's bipartite cubic planar domination conjecture
context.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite cubic planar graph, and let $\gamma(G)$ denote its domination number. **Abrishami, Henning, and Rahbarnia's conjecture.**

$$
\gamma(G) \leq \frac{|V(G)|}{3}.
$$

This is described in the paper as a weaker version of Zhu and Wu's conjecture; the source gives no resolution of it.
context.source_name: Eun-Kyung Cho, Eric Culver, Stephen G. Hartke and Vesna Iršič, “Domination of subcubic planar graphs with large girth”, arXiv:2312.03384 (2023).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03384

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2023). “It is now known that the conjecture is false in general, but Henning and Dorbec showed that it holds for graphs with girth at least $9$.”

context.title: Zhu and Wu's domination conjecture for 2-connected cubic planar graphs
context.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a $2$-connected cubic planar graph. Write $V(G)$ for its vertex set and let $\gamma(G)$ be the domination number of $G$, the minimum size of a dominating set. **Zhu and Wu's conjecture.**

$$
\gamma(G) \leq \frac{|V(G)|}{3}.
$$

The conjecture is presented as an analogue of Reed's conjecture for planar graphs. The paper reports that no counterexamples are known when the condition of $2$-connectedness is removed.
context.source_name: Eun-Kyung Cho, Eric Culver, Stephen G. Hartke and Vesna Iršič, “Domination of subcubic planar graphs with large girth”, arXiv:2312.03384 (2023).

context.title: Non-polynomial growth for k-dominating independent sets in incidence graphs of projective planes
context.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the family of incidence graphs of projective planes, and let $\text{mi}_k(n,\mathcal{F})$ denote the maximum number of $k$-dominating independent sets among $n$-vertex graphs in this family.

**Projective-plane incidence-graph conjecture.** The function $\text{mi}_k(n,\mathcal{F})$ is not bounded above by any polynomial in $n$.

This addresses the growth-rate alternatives posed for structured graph families and predicts superpolynomially many $k$-dominating independent sets in incidence graphs of projective planes. The source gives no resolution.
context.mathematics: Superpolynomial lower bound requires an infinite sequence of actual projective planes and k-dominating independent sets. No uniform independent family construction; fixed-plane counting cannot resolve growth.

context.title: Rank-symmetric nearly equal chain decomposition conjecture for the Boolean lattice
context.literal:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. A **rank-symmetric chain** in the Boolean lattice $2^{[n]}$ is a chain whose numbers of elements in complementary ranks are equal.

**Rank-symmetric chain conjecture.** The Boolean lattice $2^{[n]}$ can be partitioned into $\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ rank-symmetric chains such that the size of any two chains differ by at most $2$.

This is proposed as a rank-symmetric variant of Füredi's conjecture. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

context.literal_statement:
Let $d$ be a positive integer. A **$d$-dimensional permutation** is an $[n]^{d+1}$ array of zeros and ones with exactly one $1$ on every line parallel to any coordinate axis. For a box $\mathcal T=T_1\times\cdots\times T_{d+1}\subseteq[n]^{d+1}$, define its volume and the number of permutation entries it contains by

$$
\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal T)=\prod_i|T_i|,\qquad A(\mathcal T)=|\{\alpha\in\mathcal T:A(\alpha)=1\}|.
$$

**High-dimensional permutation discrepancy conjecture.** For every $d\geq2$ there exist arbitrarily large $d$-dimensional permutations $A$ such that, for every box $\mathcal T$,

$$
\left|A(\mathcal T)-\frac{\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal T)}{n}\right|=O(\sqrt{\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal T)}).
$$

This is a high-dimensional analogue of the expander mixing lemma and predicts optimal square-root discrepancy for all boxes. The paper gives heuristic motivation but no resolution of the conjecture.
context.ordinary_derivation_or_exact_gap: A group-table Latin construction is not enough: on an additive subgroup H of size h, the box H^3 has h^2 entries versus h^3/n expectation, exceeding a fixed multiple of h^(3/2) when h grows and h/n stays bounded below1. This rules out that naive construction, not existence of other permutations. All-box square-root bound remains unpaid.
